title: Divisive Normalization Shapes Low-Rank Slow Manifolds for Continuous Working Memory
abstract: arXiv:2608.01947v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The ability to robustly maintain and update continuous variables is a hallmark of working memory. While classical continuous attractor networks suffer from severe fine-tuning fragility, standard artificial recurrent neural networks (RNNs) like GRUs and LSTMs typically fail to stably learn continuous manifolds, instead shattering the state space into discretized point attractors. To bridge this gap, we draw inspiration from divisive normalization, a canonical neural computation widely observed across cortical circuits, and propose the Recurrent Divisive Normalization Network (RDNN), a minimal and algebraically isolated model of dynamic division. Through dynamical systems analysis on canonical working memory tasks, we demonstrate that this biophysical constraint allows the network to converge to robust, high-fidelity slow manifolds. translated_title: 除法归一化塑造用于连续工作记忆的低秩慢流形
translated_abstract: 摘要：稳健地维持和更新连续变量是工作记忆的一个标志性特征。虽然经典的连续吸引子网络存在严重的微调脆弱性，但标准的循环神经网络（如GRU和LSTM）通常无法稳定学习连续流形，反而会将状态空间破碎成离散的点吸引子。为弥合这一差距，我们从除法归一化中汲取灵感——这是一种在皮层回路中广泛观察到的典型神经计算——并提出了循环除法归一化网络（RDNN），这是一个最小且代数上孤立的动态除法模型。通过对典型工作记忆任务的动力系统分析，我们证明了这种生物物理约束使网络能够收敛到稳健、高保真的慢流形。此外，我们分析了在反向传播过程中除法归一化的梯度动态。
tldr: 本文提出循环除法归一化网络（RDNN），通过引入生物启发的除法归一化约束，使网络能稳定学习连续工作记忆的慢流形，避免了传统RNN中的离散化问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the Recurrent Divisive Normalization Network (RDNN), which leverages biophysically inspired divisive normalization to enable stable learning of continuous slow manifolds for working memory, overcoming the discretization issues of standard RNNs.
